summary: @servicetitan/schema-comparison 0.1.6 preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime ZIP from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<platform>.zip, extracts it to a temporary directory, marks it executable, and invokes it via execFileSync against a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB '@bun @bun-cjs' bundle with obfuscator.io-style transforms (hex-named identifiers, a large numeric/string array, a string-array rotator), sha256 9fc2570b7cef51c1b8df116d144d11ff4096357be7d2c4c6367cfc2509cf1bcc. The package's advertised functionality is SQL schema comparison, implemented cleanly in src/app.ts and dist/app.js; neither the legitimate source tree nor the compiled CLI references setup.mjs or math_init.js. The obfuscated payload is only reachable via the preinstall hook, executed by a freshly downloaded alternate runtime rather than Node, which bypasses tooling that inspects only Node-resolved code. package.json declares publishConfig.access='restricted' yet 0.1.6 was published publicly, consistent with a scope compromise where a preinstall dropper and obfuscated payload were grafted on top of an otherwise legitimate internal codebase.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
